gaps.sentence: 'The flight leaves now,' the announcer said. The announcer said that the flight left ___.
gaps.explanation: Now becomes then in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget to lock up,' my mother said. My mother reminded me ___ up.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' corresponds to remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'The delay is your fault,' the manager said to her. The manager ___ her for the delay.
gaps.explanation: Blame takes the pattern blame somebody for something.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.
